comment: Deliberate breakages of rules the release gates claim to enforce.
Each entry names the gate that must fail when the rule is removed.
Run with: python tools/mutate.py
`find` must appear exactly once in `file`; if it does not, the mutation
reports NOT_APPLIED rather than passing, because a manifest that has
drifted from the code tests nothing.
`expect_gate` is matched as a substring of the failing test's full name, so
it may name a distinctive fragment — but it should name the whole gate,
because a fragment can be a prefix of a second gate and then either one
satisfies the entry. Three runner defects used to force shortened values
here and are now fixed: names were cut at the first apostrophe, output was
decoded with the console codepage (so `gate: every kind × terminal cell`
could never match), and files were restored through `Path.write_text`,
which rewrote LF as CRLF. That last one was the worst of the three: with
`*.zig text eol=lf` in `.gitattributes`, `git diff` normalises CRLF away
and shows nothing, while `cmd_job.zig`'s adjacency gate reads its own
source and ends a function body at "\n}\n" — so a corrupted tree failed
that gate under the *next* mutation's name. The runner now restores by
bytes and verifies the restored file against what it read, aborting the
run if it differs.
Deleted entry, recorded so nobody reads its absence as the rule lapsing:
`v11-live-dest-unique` mutation-tested the UNIQUE on
`idx_checkpoints_live_dest` (src/core/store/migrate.zig:511), the index
that keeps two in-flight transfers off one destination. That is no longer
a gate's job. `migrate.frozenStatement` (src/core/store/migrate.zig:621)
slices the statement out of the v11 migration text at comptime — a
`std.mem.indexOf` for the literal `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX
idx_checkpoints_live_dest`, `orelse @compileError` — on behalf of
`checkpoints_index_ddl` (src/core/store/migrate.zig:651). So weakening or
removing the index stops the build. Verified rather than assumed: dropping
`UNIQUE` from line 511 reports `no frozen statement starts with: CREATE
UNIQUE INDEX idx_checkpoints_live_dest` at migrate.zig:628, referenced
from the schema-shape drift gate. A rule the compiler refuses is stronger
than one a test catches, and a mutation that cannot compile proves nothing
about a gate either way — so the entry was deleted, not repaired. (It had
also become unrunnable for a second reason: its `find` text now appears
twice in migrate.zig, once in the DDL and once in the `frozenStatement`
call that pins it, which is why it reported NOT_APPLIED rather than
BUILD_ERROR.)
Unanchored gate, recorded so nobody reads its absence as the rule lapsing:
`gate: the daemon reply path's peak allocation does not grow with the
output` (src/core/daemon/protocol_test.zig) has no entry of its own. What it
measures is `Ssh.Capture` fed in the channel's read size plus the whole
reply-building path on top; the reply-building path allocates nothing, so
every allocation the gate can see belongs to the ceiling and is already
mutation-proven one layer down by `M4-output-peak-does-not-track-the-output`
at src/core/ssh/Client.zig. The daemon-side half of the same claim — that
the daemon is asked for the bounded discipline rather than the whole reply —
is `M4d-daemon-asks-for-the-ceiling`. An entry that mutated protocol.zig
here would have to allocate from an allocator the gate does not measure, and
would report SURVIVED for a rule that is in fact enforced.

mutations.expect_gate: gate: a marker the read boundary cut in half is parsed once, whole

mutations.rule: A forward read must report where it stopped, not where it started. A cursor that never advances turns every probe into a re-read of the log from byte zero, which is unbounded traffic and re-reports markers the job has already been credited with.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the probe reads forward from its own cursor and does not start over

mutations.rule: An oversized `__TERMINUS_PROGRESS__` line is not the absence of one. Reading it as `absent` tells an agent the job reported nothing, which is the one thing that is certainly false.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a progress line is refused three ways and none of them is silence

mutations.rule: A partial line the probe refuses to store must still keep the next window off a line start. Eliding it to nothing puts the continuation of a mid-line at column zero, so `noise__TERMINUS_PROGRESS__:{...}` cut after `noise` comes back as a marker line the job never printed.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a partial line we will not store still keeps the next window off a line start

mutations.rule: The state probe may not read from the cursor that belongs to whoever is streaming output. Sharing it hands the probe whatever window the reader happened to leave behind, and every `job read` then silently changes what the next `job status` can see.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the reader's cursor and the probe's cursor never move each other

mutations.rule: What a job reported must be recorded before the window carrying it moves on. A probe that reads progress and does not store it has the value in hand at the only moment it will ever be readable.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a settled job still reports the progress it printed before it ended

mutations.rule: A probe that read must say whether it held anything back. `null` means it did not say, and `recordProbe`'s COALESCE leaves the previous fragment in place - so a carry consumed once is prepended to every window from then on.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a settled job still reports the progress it printed before it ended

mutations.rule: A job that has ended must still be able to say what it reported. Reading only the current window makes `progress` null the moment the log rotates, the session dies or the window moves past the line - which is every finished job.
mutations.find: state.progress = seen_progress orelse (if (before) |b| b.latest_progress_json else null);
mutations.expect_gate: gate: progress the probe's window has scrolled past is still what the job reported

mutations.rule: A `__TERMINUS_PROGRESS__` line that was refused may not be reported as silence. Without the note beside it, `progress` holds a true but stale value and nothing says the job's most recent statement was one we could not use.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: progress the probe's window has scrolled past is still what the job reported

mutations.rule: A sync's operation is an `exec`: its remote act is one shell script terminus composed and that script's exit status is the verdict. `cleanup`/`tunnel`/`plan_phase`/`audit` declare `judgement_undeclared` - nothing is known about what one is judged by - so filing a sync as one records a verdict the kind does not claim to have.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a sync that unpacks cleanly leaves one operation with a terminal and a findable id

mutations.rule: A sync contends on the remote directory it names, as a `.path` scope, so `scope.Scope.overlaps`'s containment arm makes a sync into /srv/app block one into /srv/app/dist and a `terminus push` aimed at /srv/app/config.json. A `.job` scope only ever matches an identical key and sees no transfer at all.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a submitted sync push holds its remote directory, and a read-only pull does not

mutations.rule: `--dry-run` changes nothing, so its attempt must be `mutating = false` and hold no barrier; a real push must hold one. Dropping the negation inverts both: the preview bars the run it previews, and the run that replaces a directory bars nobody.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: --dry-run records a read-only attempt, settles it, and bars nobody

mutations.rule: A run settled `indeterminate` is unknown whatever number is sitting beside it. Reading the exit code without first reading the status turns a lost answer into a clean sync.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: verdictOf never turns an outcome nobody reported into an answer

mutations.rule: A channel that broke after the script went out, or closed without the supervisor's exit marker, reports no exit status. Defaulting that to zero reports a sync push - which runs `rm -rf` and `tar -xf` - as completed on the strength of a number nobody sent.
mutations.find:
if (outcome.status == .indeterminate) return .unknown;
    const code = outcome.exit_code orelse return .unknown;
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a sync whose answer never arrived settles indeterminate, never failed

mutations.rule: A `push --dry-run` connected and chose not to submit: `local_abandon` (cancelled) is the terminal for that. `never_submitted` records `failed` and claims a transport error that never happened, for a run that did exactly what it was asked.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: --dry-run records a read-only attempt, settles it, and bars nobody

mutations.rule: The host's `exit 43` means it read a digest that did not match and unpacked nothing. Folding that into the success arm reports `ok: true` for a transfer that was refused.
mutations.replace: if (code == 0 or code == corrupt_exit) return .{ .completed = outcome.stdout };
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a remote extract the host refused settles a failure and is never read as success

mutations.rule: The refusal code the unpack script uses for a digest mismatch must not be zero: the host would print `checksum mismatch` and exit 0, which every reader of an exit status takes for a clean unpack.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the unpack script proves the digest before it destroys anything

mutations.rule: `doctor` opens no operation, and the reason is that its probe changes nothing: every write is a zero-byte file at a fixed terminus-named path removed on the same shell line. A `touch` that outlives the command is a change to the host with no request id.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: doctor's probe changes nothing, which is why it opens no operation

mutations.rule: `server ping` opens no operation, and the reason is that the whole of what it sends is `true` - the POSIX no-op. Any command with an effect there is a remote change nothing in the ledger describes.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: `server ping` sends a command that cannot change the host

mutations.rule: An agent that meets exit 75 from a `sync push` must be told to reconcile rather than retry: the retry runs `rm -rf` on the destination a second time. The document is the only place that sentence exists.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the skill document describes the receipt a sync now leaves

mutations.rule: A remote command built from an argv must render every element as exactly one shell word, never join them raw.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: an argv element with a space, a quote, a $ and braces is one shell word

mutations.rule: A daemon that did not answer may not be reported as a container that does not exist. Five absences, five readings.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: each distinguishable failure is reported as itself and not as another

mutations.rule: A health wait whose deadline expires may never report the target as reached.
mutations.find: return finish(.timed_out, probe, polls, waited, null);
mutations.replace: return finish(.reached, probe, polls, waited, null);
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a wait whose deadline expires is timed_out, and timed_out is not success

mutations.rule: A running container whose image declares no HEALTHCHECK can never become healthy, and must be refused rather than waited on.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a running container with no HEALTHCHECK cannot reach healthy, and says so

mutations.rule: Only the target state may satisfy a wait for that target.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: no combination reports the target reached except the target itself

mutations.rule: A reading that is not a container state may not be published with ok: true.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: every vocabulary key takes a word from its own closed list

mutations.rule: The published --json key set of `docker wait` is pinned; a key added, renamed or reordered must fail rather than ship.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the published key sets are exactly these, and only two of them are prose

mutations.rule: A job control act contends on a scope of its own. On the job's own scope, `execution.begin` is refused by the very attempt the kill is aimed at, `settleAndForgetJob` reads the control row as the peer blocking its own removal, and an `indeterminate` control row bars the job for good.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a job control act contends on a scope of its own, never the job's

mutations.rule: A session the host reports still present after `kill-session` settles the control act `proven_failure`, never a cancellation: `cancelled` there publishes a stopped shell over one that is still running.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a control act's terminal is the host's answer, and both answers are admissible

mutations.rule: Every branch that sends `kill-session` records what the host answered onto this command's own control operation, on the line after the kill.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a kill of a finished job leaves one settled control operation beside the job's own

mutations.rule: A reporter that ends the process settles this command's control operation itself. `Cli.exitNow` and `Cli.failIndeterminateAfterOutput` settle nothing, so a control row left there is unsettled for good.
mutations.find:
abandonControl(control, controlWithheld(ctx, authority, job.name));
    // Before the document, and that ordering is the rule on every branch of both
mutations.replace: // Before the document, and that ordering is the rule on every branch of both
mutations.expect_gate: gate: every reporter that can end the process records or abandons the control act

mutations.rule: `job receipt` publishes what was observed *and* what a later reconcile proved. Collapsing `status` onto `effectiveStatus` erases the disagreement the `status` / `resolved_status` pair exists to keep.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: job receipt reports an unsettled attempt as unsettled, and a resolved one as both

mutations.rule: `job receipt` publishes the redacted command rather than nothing. The gate beside this one asserts that no credential reaches the document; on its own that would also pass over an empty document, so the redacted form has to be there for the absence to mean redaction.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: job receipt carries no secret, and its --json key set is pinned

mutations.rule: `job receipt --json`'s key set is pinned in both directions with a count, including which keys are nullable. A never-null key that quietly becomes nullable changes what every caller must handle, and no compiler catches it: the initialiser coerces.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: job receipt carries no secret, and its --json key set is pinned

mutations.rule: A handoff whose section failed is never `complete`. Dropping a section and still claiming completeness is the pseudo-success class this verb exists to refuse.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a section this build refuses to read leaves complete false and names itself

mutations.rule: A section nobody could read has no provenance. Naming one would let an empty section pass for a read one.
mutations.find: const unread: Reading = .{ .answered = false, .source = null, .observedAt = null, .count = 0 };
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a section this build refuses to read leaves complete false and names itself

mutations.rule: No section that describes the host may report `live`: a handoff asks the host nothing, so every host-describing section is a dated cache.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: every section is answered with its own observedAt, and only errors is live

mutations.rule: A job's freshness is when the host was last probed, never when the row was written. The schema puts `last_probed_at` there for this reader so a stale reading cannot pass for a live one.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: every section is answered with its own observedAt, and only errors is live

mutations.rule: Every string entering a handoff goes through the sole redactor. A memory is authored free text and the likeliest place a credential is written down.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a secret in every reachable column reaches no field of the document

mutations.rule: `operations.argv_redacted` is redacted again at the document boundary. The column has many writers and a handoff is a release blocker, so its contract is not taken on trust.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a secret in every reachable column reaches no field of the document

mutations.rule: A handoff never emits an argv that overrides a peer's live claim. A lease it read out of a cache is not grounds for telling a reader to force it.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: every resume argv runs as written, and the dishonest ones carry none

mutations.rule: Only an adoptable checkpoint is resumable. A parked publish still holds its destination and may already have landed, so offering to send the bytes again would overwrite a result nobody has judged.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: an unjudged publish is reconciled, never sent again

mutations.rule: A section that could not be enumerated says so. Reporting zero checkpoints for a ledger that could not be read would hide a destination-holding transfer behind a plausible empty list.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a ledger that cannot be read takes transfers with it, under its own name

mutations.rule: The published --json key set of `handoff` is pinned; a key added, renamed or reordered must fail rather than ship.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the published key set is exactly this, and the section names are the vocabulary

mutations.rule: A handoff reads the server row directly and never resolves auth: `Cli.resolveServer` loads private key material, and a verb that dials stops working in the one situation this one exists for.
mutations.find:
const server = (Store.servers.getByName(&store, ctx.arena, server_name) catch |err|
        Cli.storeFatal(&store, err)) orelse fatal("unknown server '{s}'", .{server_name});
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a handoff reaches no host, so an offline one answers every section

mutations.rule: A memory with no grant is untrusted. That is the whole boundary in front of `verify_cmd`: the command text arrives by `terminus import` from documents anybody can hand over, and a row that reads as trusted without a grant makes handing somebody a snapshot equivalent to arbitrary code execution on their hosts.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: an untrusted verify command is not run, no connection is opened, and the refusal names the grant

mutations.rule: A grant authorises the exact command text it was given. Without the digest comparison a grant is a flag, and a flag keeps applying after the text changes under it - trust `systemctl is-active nginx`, then rewrite --verify-cmd to a pipe-to-shell on the same key and the flag is still set. The digest is what makes that laundering unreachable without any writer having to remember to revoke.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a grant covers the text it was given and nothing else

mutations.rule: An unauthorised verify command is refused with nothing *opened*, not merely with nothing sent. The connection is a `Dial` the driver asks for rather than something it already holds, precisely so the refusal is a claim about what was done and not about what was written to a channel that was already up.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: an untrusted verify command is not run, no connection is opened, and the refusal names the grant

mutations.rule: A refusal that cannot say what to do next is one an operator can only obey. The refusal renders the exact `memory trust` command line that would authorise this memory's command, by --key or by --id; naming any other verb sends the operator to a read that changes nothing.
mutations.find: return std.fmt.allocPrint(arena, "terminus memory trust {s} --key {s}", .{ target, key });
mutations.replace: return std.fmt.allocPrint(arena, "terminus memory show {s} --key {s}", .{ target, key });
mutations.expect_gate: gate: an untrusted verify command is not run, no connection is opened, and the refusal names the grant

mutations.rule: A verify command that runs and disagrees is not an observation. Recording one would make a contradicted memory read as freshly confirmed, which is worse than reading as stale. An exit code is never negative, so comparing against `< 0` records every disagreement as a live reading.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a command that disagrees is not recorded as an observation

mutations.rule: An import carries `observed_at` verbatim. The document's claim about when the fact was seen is the whole reason to move a memory between machines; substituting the moment of the import turns every imported note into a fresh one, which is the write-time-as-observation confusion v13 exists to remove.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: observed_at survives an export/import round trip unchanged

mutations.rule: How this store came to hold a fact is not the document's to say. An imported row is `legacy_import` - it was read out of a file - and labelling it `cache` claims somebody here wrote it down after looking at the host.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: observed_at survives an export/import round trip unchanged

mutations.rule: The export document has no field for a trust grant, in either direction. A field it could parse is a field a crafted document could fill, and `ignore_unknown_fields` only discards what the type has no key for. The field counts are asserted so that adding one is a decision somebody has to come and write down.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: no wire type or insert option can carry a trust grant

mutations.rule: The backfilled observation says it is one. `observed_at` for a pre-v13 row is `updated_at` - a write time standing in for an observation - and the column default is what labels it. Defaulting to any other member makes every row that nobody has observed claim a reading it never took, which is precisely the confusion the version exists to remove.
mutations.find: \\ALTER TABLE memories ADD COLUMN observed_source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'backfill'
mutations.replace: \\ALTER TABLE memories ADD COLUMN observed_source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'cache'
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a memory written before v13 is backfilled and the row says it was

mutations.rule: Every predicate in `grant_is_whole` is `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` before it is anything else, because a CHECK whose expression evaluates to NULL *passes*. A bare inequality on `trusted_by` is NULL on the row where `trusted_by` is missing, so the constraint admits exactly the half-grant it exists to refuse: a timestamp and a digest with nobody's name against them.
mutations.find: \\        AND trusted_by IS NOT NULL AND trusted_by <> ''
mutations.expect_gate: gate: half a trust grant cannot be stored

mutations.rule: The four sources Zig can write are the four the column admits. The schema's copy of a vocabulary and the Zig one are written out twice on purpose and nothing derives one from the other, so a member the column accepts and `memories.observed_sources` cannot name is a row `list` refuses to read back.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the observation sources Zig can write are the ones the memories column admits

mutations.rule: The `cd` a job is launched with is composed in one place. `Tmux.jobLaunchLine` and `cmd_exec.runOneShot` each held a copy of `"cd {s} && ({s})"` taking `--cwd` or the server workspace, and neither quoted it; a directory holding a space rendered `cd /srv/two words`, which a POSIX shell answers `cd: too many arguments`, so the `&&` never fired and the attempt settled `exited` code 1 for a command that was never sent. The per-file exemption on this file covered that placeholder under reasons written about session names and ULIDs.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: every raw value Tmux.zig sends to a host is exempted by name and reason

mutations.rule: A `--exclude` pattern is one shell word. `pull` built `" --exclude='*{s}*'"` from values `parseExcludes` only trims whitespace from, so the quotes belonged to the template and escaped nothing: a pattern holding an apostrophe ended that word early and the rest of it became syntax in the middle of a `tar` command line. The same file has validated the sibling argument of that template since an earlier audit.
mutations.find:
const value = try std.mem.concat(arena, u8, &.{ "--exclude=*", pattern, "*" });
    return std.fmt.allocPrint(arena, "{f}", .{Core.shell.word(value)});
mutations.expect_gate: gate: every --exclude pattern is one shell word, and the archive script proves it

mutations.rule: `cd` gets `--` before its operand. Quoting does not stop `cd` reading its argument as an option: `cd '-P'` is `cd -P`, which takes no operand and succeeds *in the home directory*, reporting nothing wrong — a working directory silently different from the one asked for.
mutations.expect_gate: cdInto composes one command, and the directory in it is one word

mutations.rule: A working directory is rendered as exactly one shell word. `Cwd.format` recognises the two spellings of the remote home itself and quotes every byte the operator wrote; writing the value out raw is the original defect, and `cd: too many arguments` is a proven failure recorded against a command that never ran.
mutations.find: const rest = homeRemainder(c.raw) orelse return word(c.raw).format(writer);
mutations.replace: const rest = homeRemainder(c.raw) orelse return writer.writeAll(c.raw);
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a working directory a shell would have refused reaches the host as one word

mutations.rule: A working directory that was relying on the remote shell expanding it is refused rather than quietly turned into a literal path. `Cwd` performs exactly one expansion — a leading `~` or `$HOME` — so `$RELEASE/app` is now a directory nobody has, and a `cd` that fails settles an exit code for a command that never ran.
mutations.find:
if (std.mem.indexOfScalar(u8, rest, '$') != null)
        return "it contains `$`, and terminus expands only a leading `~` or `" ++ home_expansion ++ "`";
mutations.replace:
if (std.mem.indexOfScalar(u8, rest, 0) != null)
        return "it contains `$`, and terminus expands only a leading `~` or `" ++ home_expansion ++ "`";
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a working directory that cannot keep its meaning is refused, not rendered quietly

mutations.rule: `exec` refuses an unusable working directory before `execution.begin`, which is the only point at which a refusal costs nothing: once the operation row exists the attempt has to be settled, and there is no honest terminal for declining to compose the command.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a working directory that lost its expansion is refused before anything is recorded

mutations.rule: The `sync` history row's exit code is the attempt's own status. It was a hardcoded `0` and that was reachable on the indeterminate path: `push`'s `.unknown` arm returns rather than fatals, so the row was written and only then did the verb exit 75 — `terminus history --json` showed `"exit_code": 0` for a sync that may or may not have run `rm -rf` on the destination. `history.Record.exit_code` is `?i64 = null`.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the sync history row reports no exit code when nothing answered

mutations.rule: `docker wait --interval` is held inside [1s, 1h]. `waitFor` sleeps `interval_secs` seconds and a sleep of zero is not a sleep, so `--interval 0` issued `docker container inspect` over the SSH channel as fast as the channel could carry it for the whole of `--timeout`. The gates below `waitFor` pass zero deliberately so they do not sleep, which is why the clamp is at the flag. Same bounds and same reason as `cmd_job.parseInterval`.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: --interval cannot make a watch busy-spin, and cannot outlast its deadline

mutations.rule: A redaction that could not be performed is reported, not worked around. This was the only arm in the tree that wrote unredacted text on purpose; its sharpest form was inside one function, where `cmd_sync.run` refuses to store a detail string unredacted for the ledger and then handed the same bytes to a call that stored them raw on allocation failure.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a redaction that could not be performed refuses rather than storing raw

mutations.rule: The remote directory is a `shell.Word` in every script `sync` sends, not a value inside quotes the template owns. `validateRemotePath` admits a space, a `;`, a `|` and a `&`, which were harmless only because of those quotes — the arrangement that has failed in this project seven times.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: cmd_sync's script builders splice no value raw, and its excludes are words

mutations.rule: `job start` refuses an unexpandable --cwd before `execution.begin`, `jobs.create` and `Tmux.ensure` — all three. Removing the check makes a $RELEASE/app a literal path, the `cd` fail, and the attempt settle an exit code for a command that never ran, with a job row and a live tmux session behind it.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a working directory that lost its expansion is refused before all three side effects

mutations.rule: A reply that stopped part-way is a broken connection, not a peer speaking another protocol version.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a CLI that finds no daemon gets a named refusal, never a hang and never a wrong cause

mutations.rule: A header this build could read, whose frame did not arrive whole, is FrameIncomplete; only bytes that are not a frame header at all are MalformedFrame, and only those are a version skew.
mutations.find:
error.OutOfMemory => return error.OutOfMemory,
        error.EndOfStream => return error.FrameIncomplete,
mutations.replace:
error.OutOfMemory => return error.OutOfMemory,
        error.EndOfStream => return error.MalformedFrame,
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a CLI that finds no daemon gets a named refusal, never a hang and never a wrong cause

mutations.rule: A write to the staging partial that the disk refuses ends the transfer; it is never counted as a slice that arrived.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a local disk that fills mid-transfer keeps the destination and confirms no more than it took

mutations.rule: A push's arrived count is what the host took, never the size it was asked for.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a host that runs out of space mid-push never sends a command that names the destination

mutations.rule: No field of a published document carries a default, so a branch that omits a key does not compile.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: no published document has a field with a default, in any of the six modules

mutations.rule: The receipt document's status keys carry a word from op_state.Status and from nothing else.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the receipt document's shape is pinned at the depth each key is at

mutations.rule: A key the ledger holds a value for is published with that value; a null there reports an absence over a fact.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the receipt document's shape is pinned at the depth each key is at

mutations.rule: The memories section dates itself by the observation, never by the write. Reading `updated_at` makes a six-month-old note look as fresh as the moment somebody last re-tagged it, which is the distinction v13 exists to record.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the memories section dates itself by the observation, not the write
